question: How much knowledge and problem-solving ability do pretrained language models have across many academic and professional subjects, measured zero- and few-shot?
hypothesis: Pretrained models should hold broad world knowledge from their corpora, and a broad multi-subject exam in zero/few-shot form exposes blind spots that narrower benchmarks miss.
contributions: A 57-task multiple-choice benchmark (MMLU) spanning elementary to professional level
Evaluation of GPT-3 (four sizes) and UnifiedQA showing near-chance accuracy except for the largest GPT-3
Analysis of lopsided per-subject performance, calibration and weakness on calculation and on law/morality

method.summary: Questions were hand-collected by students from free online sources (GRE, USMLE practice, course and OUP-reader questions) into 57 subjects, split into dev/val/test. Pretrained or transfer models are scored by 4-way multiple-choice accuracy with a fixed zero- or few-shot prompt; no training on the test.

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.split: 5 per subject dev (few-shot), 1540 validation, 14079 test; at least 100 test examples per subject
datasets.source: Freely available online sources collected by graduate and undergraduate students
datasets.preprocessing: Math expressions encoded in LaTeX or symbols such as * and ^

datasets.name: UnifiedQA training data / MMLU dev+val
datasets.source: Used to fine-tune RoBERTa-base, ALBERT-xxlarge, GPT-2 (App A.1)

models.name: UnifiedQA
models.init_from: T5, fine-tuned on prior QA datasets

inference.decoding: Take the highest-probability among tokens A, B, C, D after 'Answer: '
inference.samples: one deterministic pass per item; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Header 'The following are multiple choice questions (with answers) about [subject].', up to 5 fixed dev-set demonstrations, then the question, ending in 'Answer: '. Zero-shot has no demonstrations. UnifiedQA input: QUESTION \n (A) .. (B) .. </s>, lowercased; prediction = class with highest token overlap with output.

other.fine_tuned_baselines: RoBERTa-base, ALBERT-xxlarge, GPT-2 fine-tuned to predict one of four classes; hyperparameters not stated
other.law_experiment: about 2,000 extra Professional Law training examples; RoBERTa-base continued pretraining on about 1.6M case summaries

metrics.definition: classification accuracy across all examples and tasks (weighted average per discipline)

metrics.name: RMS calibration error
metrics.definition: root mean squared gap between confidence and accuracy

eval.protocol: Single run per model; no significance tests; validation set may be used for hyperparameters, test for final accuracy.

limits: Text-only; authors note multimodal knowledge is untested and propose a 'Turk Test'.
Contamination checked only indirectly (log-prob vs accuracy correlation, Fig 13); authors concede models saw related Wikipedia text and promise a list of question sources.
Only GPT-3 via API and UnifiedQA evaluated at scale; no training details of GPT-3 given, so size effects are confounded with pretraining data.
Single runs, no variance; UnifiedQA is sensitive to format (removing </s> costs several points; Moral Scenarios format hurts it).
Expert accuracy of 89.8% is partly an educated guess.
Ground-truth label quality not audited; has dated: frontier models now far exceed 43.9% (not in the source).
